items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: I knew what he wanted because I did my homework and I wasn’t going to try to do my Roy Haynes imitation behind Arnett Cobb.

ctx.x: What was that like — not only musically but socially and generationally. How did he speak to you about what he wanted?

Oh he didn’t. I was known as “Little Eddie” because all the guys that I played with when I was coming up — Arnett was — I knew what he wanted because I did my homework and I wasn’t going to try to do my Roy Haynes imitation behind Arnett Cobb. Straight ahead, straight ahead. He was very kind, a man who endured unbelievable pain because of that horrible accident he had. How he stayed on the stage on those crutches or sitting on the stool all night, never went to the men’s room, because it was so difficult for him…
